data.goal: Make every batch F-7 publishes durable (Room row + per-batch files under ~/.rectify) and surface it as the third, desktop-only segment of RectifyWindow's inspector tab strip: a LazyColumn of Today/Yesterday/Older-grouped rows with a union-bbox thumbnail, title, meta line and status chip, plus an In-progress badge and a 'claude · session <id>' footer — without a new Gradle module, a new design-system component, or any change to F-7's merged wire contract.
data.problemStatement: PER-2 (QA tester) has no durable record of batches already sent to the coding agent. FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.publish prunes every handoff-slot directory except the newest and data-handoff-api states verbatim 'No history, no ring buffer, no expiry', so the previous send's images vanish on the next send and nothing at all survives an app restart. There is therefore no way to see what has already been reported and in what state without re-testing, and F-9's Verify loop has no durable original frame to diff against.
data.highLevelDescription: One persistence vertical hung off the existing mirror surface. Write path: MirrorViewModel.resolveAndSend() already holds `frozen`, `held.bitmap`, `held.bytes` and, after assembly, `(envelope, images)` as in-memory locals; inside the SAME withContext(Dispatchers.Default) assembly block it additionally crops AND downscales the union bounding box of the batch's annotation rects to <=128px and hands that small ImageBitmap to the existing CropEncoder, producing a few-KB thumbnail PNG. On `published.onSuccess`, BEFORE postSideEffect(SendComplete), the VM calls `recordSentBatch(...): Result<Unit>` and consumes it with `.onFailure { log.w }` and nothing else — the persist lives in its own failure domain and can never touch SendPhase. Down the stack RecordSentBatchUseCaseImpl → HistoryRepositoryImpl writes bulk bytes through a `fun interface BatchFileStore` (desktop java.io, null-returning stand-in elsewhere, never throws) to ~/.rectify/history/<sanitised batchId>/{frame.png, crop-N.png, hierarchy.xml}, then inserts the parent row plus normalised history_annotation children in one @Transaction with whatever paths the store returned (or null). Read path: HistoryEntryDao exposes Flow<List<HistoryEntryWithAnnotations>> ordered sentAtMs DESC → HistoryEntryMapper.toModel → ObserveHistoryUseCase (bare Flow) → collected once in MirrorViewModel's container init into MirrorUiState.history, which feeds both the list and the badge. Render path: MirrorHistoryTab = Column { LazyColumn(weight(1f)) { group headers + HistoryRow items keyed by entry id }; footer }, grouping computed at render time by pure groupHistory(entries, nowMs, zone); the few-KB BLOB is decoded inside a remember(entry.id) so the list performs zero filesystem reads and no repeat decodes. Two edits in RectifyWindow.kt close the loop.
data.background: F-7 (resolve-and-send-mcp) is merged and ships AnnotationHandoff/AnnotationEnvelope, mintSessionId, EnvelopeAssembly and CropEncoder. ShellTab.History, the Cmd+3 shortcut, SidebarTabs' per-tab count, HistoryRow, StatusPill/StatusPillTone and AppButtonSize.ListAction are all already built and registered — only the panel body (`else -> Unit` in RectifyWindow.kt) and all persistence are missing. data-database-impl is a live but never-instantiated Room skeleton: AppDatabase is a lazy Koin single nothing injects, and neither ~/rectify.db nor ~/.rectify/ exists on disk, which is what makes relocating the DB and staying at @Database(version = 1) safe and makes Step 0 a blocking spike.

assumptions: AS-1: a single integration point (the resolveAndSend call site) is sufficient to trigger the persist; F-8 never polls or reads back the handoff slot.
AS-2: AC-22's 'title/summary' is the batch's first annotation's comment text — no separate generated summary field.
AS-3: the static 'claude' agent label is acceptable; mcp-application ships exactly one tool and one consumer.
AS-4: Sent shares Verified's neutral (StatusPillTone.Neutral / ink3) tone until product says otherwise.
AS-29: BatchFileStore never throws and returns null on any failure; Android/iOS bind a null-returning stand-in, unreachable in practice because UnsupportedAnnotationHandoff.publish throws first.
AS-30: assembly, crop encoding and the thumbnail encode all run inside the existing withContext(Dispatchers.Default) boundaries already documented in resolveAndSend's KDoc.

PLAN-AS-1 (CONFIRMED AT REFINE by reading CropWindow.kt): cropWindow uses designPad = 14f, boxW = 84f, boxH = 72f, designWidth = 296f and returns a CropWindow(srcOffset/srcSize/dstSize/scale/outlineRect) render window, not PNG bytes. It is NOT reused for the thumbnail. FR-29's pad=18 / bw=bh=40 is the prototype's crop() formula; the plan reimplements it as a pure thumbnailRect(union, frameSize, designPad = 18f, designWidth = 296f) in core/history/, keeping cropWindow's design-space pad-scaling convention (pad = designPad * frameWidth / designWidth) verbatim.

PLAN-AS-2 (CONFIRMED AT REFINE by repo-wide grep): zero `pluralStringResource` usages and zero `<plurals>` resources exist in any source file — the only hits are inside this spec's own SDD documents. The note count ships as two plain keys (mirror_history_meta_note_one / mirror_history_meta_note_other) selected by a pure function; no 's' is hand-concatenated and no plural API is introduced.

PLAN-AS-3 (CONFIRMED AT REFINE, and stronger than the draft claimed): SidebarTabs renders `if (item.count != null) Text(item.count.toString())`, so a present-but-zero count would paint a literal '0' next to the label. Omitting the ShellTab.History key from tabCounts at zero is therefore REQUIRED for AC-34, not merely defensive. tabCounts becomes a buildMap.

PLAN-AS-4 (CONFIRMED AT REFINE by reading HistoryRow.kt): `private val ThumbnailSize: Dp = 56.dp`, while the design quotes 44x44. The shipped component is reused as-is; the encoded thumbnail is capped at 128px on its longest edge so it stays crisp inside the 56dp plate at any density. Changing the plate size is a design-system change no AC requires.

PLAN-AS-5: Room's builder() does not touch the filesystem — the database file is opened on first query — so a bad path or unwritable home surfaces as a query exception inside the guarded Flow or inside resultLauncher, not as a crash while Koin constructs the graph.
PLAN-AS-6: the batch directory name is batchId.replace(Regex("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"), "_") because mintSessionId embeds a device id that is not guaranteed filesystem-safe.
PLAN-AS-7: the row's id is the envelope's sessionId; a same-millisecond collision on the same device+frame degrades to an overwrite via @Insert(onConflict = REPLACE) rather than a crash.

PLAN-AS-8 (C-1 RESOLVED AT REFINE — decision of record, no fork left open): AwtCropEncoder crops only (`frame.toAwtImage().getSubimage(...)`), never scales, so handing it a union rect over a 1080x2400 frame really does yield a ~250 KB PNG. The fix stands and is viable in commonMain: `ImageBitmap(w, h)`, `androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Canvas(image: ImageBitmap)` and `Canvas.drawImageRect(image, srcOffset, srcSize, dstOffset, dstSize, paint)` are all commonMain compose-ui-graphics API, and `Paint().filterQuality = FilterQuality.Medium` gives the downsample filter. The scaled ImageBitmap is then handed to the UNCHANGED CropEncoder with rect = the scaled bitmap's full bounds, so NO new DI seam, no new expect/actual and no CropEncoder signature change appears. It is also strictly cheaper than the naive path: AwtCropEncoder calls toAwtImage() on whatever it is given, so passing a 128px bitmap allocates a ~64 KB BufferedImage instead of a ~10 MB one. The documented AWT fallback (a desktopMain sibling doing getSubimage + getScaledInstance behind a Koin qualifier) is NOT taken and is retained only as a named contingency with a single trigger: the step-7 ThumbnailBitmapTest in desktopTest failing to produce a <=128px, <=8 KB, non-null PNG off the main thread.

PLAN-AS-9 (mapper shape, corrected at refine): HistoryEntryMapper is one internal object in data-repository-impl/core/mapper/ exposing `val toModel: Mapper<HistoryEntryWithAnnotations, HistoryEntryModel>` (with the unknown-status-to-Sent fallback that earns it a named object per mappers.md) plus `fun SentBatchModel.toEntities(dirPath: String?): Pair<HistoryEntryEntity, List<HistoryAnnotationEntity>>` for the write direction. It is deliberately NOT a ModelResourceMapper: that interface pairs a mapping with its inverse, and the inverse of the READ model is not the write path (the write path starts from SentBatchModel and needs the store's dirPath). Inventing an unused toResource to satisfy the shape would be the exact dead code mappers.md's 'use a Mapper lambda/object' clause exists to avoid.

PLAN-AS-10 (datasource mixin, corrected at refine): HistoryDataSource mixes in ObservableDataSource<HistoryEntryWithAnnotations> (observeAll fits exactly) and AppendableDataSource<HistoryEntryWithAnnotations> (insert returns the implicit rowid Long, unused but harmless), and declares `suspend fun updateStatus(id: String, status: String)` itself. UpsertableDataSource is dropped — `upsert(resource): Int` has no caller.

PLAN-AS-11 (recomposition guards, added at refine): HistoryEntryModel carries a ByteArray, which compares by identity, so every Room emission produces a state the reducer cannot deduplicate — exactly the property presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md's deviation 2 warns about. At once-per-send frequency this is acceptable, but it is made bounded rather than merely rare: the LazyColumn uses `items(key = { it.id })` so an unchanged row is not recomposed, and the BLOB is decoded inside `remember(entry.id) { entry.thumbPng?.decodeToImageBitmap() }` so a recomposition never re-decodes a PNG. `decodeToImageBitmap` reaches every feature module's commonMain through FeatureConventionPlugin's compose components.resources dependency (already relied on by MirrorViewModel's frame decode).

PLAN-AS-12 (prompt provenance, added at refine from bugs.json#PP-TD-2): the persisted `prompt` column is taken from the assembled `envelope`, never from MirrorUiState.promptOverride. PP-TD-2 means a stale override can survive a ClearStaged; reading state would make History durably disagree with what the agent actually received. Taking the envelope's own field makes the record true by construction and needs no fix for PP-TD-2/PP-TD-7 to land first.

PLAN-AS-13: HistoryRow.onClick is non-nullable, so the v1 no-op row passes `onClick = {}`. The row therefore still carries Role.Button. Accepted for v1 and recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight; the row becomes genuinely clickable when F-9 adds the detail view.

constraints.text: Desktop-only (jvm target) — matches F-7's desktop-only AnnotationHandoff and RectifyWindow, the only host for the tab strip.

Must use the existing Room KMP scaffold (data-database-api/data-database-impl); F-8 is its first real consumer. KSP is already configured for kspAndroid/kspIosArm64/kspIosSimulatorArm64/kspDesktop — do not re-wire it.

Must ingest exclusively via the existing AnnotationHandoff/AnnotationEnvelope contract; AnnotationEnvelope's field order is wire-breaking and is not touched. CropEncoder's signature is likewise fixed — the thumbnail adapts to it, not the reverse.
DB relocates to ~/.rectify/rectify.db AND stays at @Database(version = 1) with no Migration — the two decisions ship together or not at all. Destructive migration is disabled repo-wide.
No new Gradle module: MirrorHost's KDoc states there is exactly one call site, and a :presentation-feature-history module would force a second koinViewModel().

No new runtime dependency: no okio, no kotlinx-io, no image library. kotlinx-datetime is already in the version catalog (one build-file line, not a new dependency); kotlinx-coroutines-test is already in the catalog and already wired in data-repository-impl.

:compose-application has NO test wiring — nothing testable may land there. Pure logic lives in presentation-feature-mirror/core/history/ (commonTest), the one bitmap helper in that module's desktopTest, repository/mapper logic in data-repository-impl (commonTest) and DAO behaviour in data-database-impl (desktopTest).
commonTest compiles for iOS: backtick test names containing a comma or a colon fail compileTestKotlinIosArm64. Plain camelCase names only (apostrophes are verified fine).
NFR-4: no network egress — all batch storage is local filesystem plus the local database; no analytics, no telemetry, no crash-report payloads carrying annotation text.
Step 0 is a blocking spike. Room has never been instantiated in this repo; no entity/DAO/repository work starts until an insert+observe round-trip is green on desktop.
Step 0 is timeboxed to half a day. A BundledSQLiteDriver packaging fight is a scope conversation with the orchestrator, not an in-branch debug session.

The spike also adds the module's missing commonTest dependency block (kotlinx-coroutines-test for runTest). risks.text: Staying at schema version 1 while changing the entity set would crash any machine that somehow already holds a v1 rectify.db.
risks.mitigation: Relocating the file to ~/.rectify/rectify.db in the same change makes a pre-existing file impossible by construction. The two decisions ship together; if the relocation is dropped, the version bump plus a Migration becomes mandatory.

risks.text: A full-resolution union-bbox crop would be hundreds of KB per row, contradicting the 'few KB BLOB' basis of the thumbnail decision and ballooning MirrorUiState at scale. Confirmed real at refine: AwtCropEncoder crops and never scales.
risks.mitigation: Resolved, not merely mitigated (PLAN-AS-8): cropAndScale the union window to <=128px on its longest edge into a scratch ImageBitmap using commonMain Canvas(ImageBitmap) + drawImageRect, and hand THAT to the unchanged CropEncoder. One encoder seam, no new DI. Converted from a hope into a check: the step-7 desktopTest asserts <=128px, non-null bytes and <=8 KB. Only that test failing triggers the AWT-sibling fallback.

risks.text: Adding two non-defaulted MirrorViewModel constructor params breaks every existing VM test until MirrorFakes is updated.
risks.mitigation: Update MirrorFakes.kt in the same commit: RecordSentBatchUseCase { Result.success(Unit) } and ObserveHistoryUseCase { emptyFlow() }. Defaults are deliberately refused — a default turns a missing Koin binding into silently losing every batch (bugs.json#PP-TD-3's exact failure shape).

risks.text: Disk + SQLite work inside resolveAndSend lengthens the send's perceived latency.
risks.mitigation: A few hundred KB on Dispatchers.IO inside an already multi-second operation, and the thumbnail path is now cheaper than the draft's (a 64 KB toAwtImage instead of a 10 MB one). Documented single-line escape hatch (detached viewModelScope.launch) if ever measured as felt; not taken now because it makes SC-16 racy against the toast.

risks.text: Growing MirrorUiState with a ByteArray-bearing list that cannot deduplicate adds reducer passes and recompositions to a pixel-sensitive state machine.
risks.mitigation: Emissions happen once per send, not once per frame, and the cost is bounded structurally rather than by frequency alone: LazyColumn items are keyed by entry id and the BLOB is decoded inside remember(entry.id) (PLAN-AS-11). This respects deviation 2 in presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md because the thumbnail stays bytes in state and is only decoded inside the row.

risks.text: Storing thumbnail bytes in the DB could be read as contradicting the closed 'paths, not BLOBs' decision.
risks.mitigation: Stated explicitly in this plan and in the entity's KDoc: frame.png and crop-N.png remain files on disk with paths in the DB exactly as decided; the BLOB is a separate derived few-KB thumbnail that exists only so a commonMain composable needs no file-reading seam.

risks.text: AC-34's badge can never be demonstrated end-to-end in F-8 because nothing ever writes In progress.
risks.mitigation: Unit-test the count-to-badge mapping (including the omit-at-zero branch) and seed one row manually in the DB during the demo. Never ship a fake transition to make a screenshot look right.

risks.text: Unbounded disk growth from retained frame/crop/hierarchy copies.
risks.mitigation: Closed, accepted ceiling (clarify decision). Marked with a `ponytail:` comment in BatchFileStore naming the upgrade path (age or count cap) rather than re-litigated.

risks.text: A failed DB insert is invisible to the user — one batch quietly missing from History.
risks.mitigation: Accepted: F-8 has no error surface and the alternative (failing the send) is explicitly ruled out. log.w carries the batch id. Cheap upgrade if it proves unacceptable: reuse the existing SendComplete snackbar path with a different summary.

risks.text: The persisted prompt could durably record a stale promptOverride (bugs.json#PP-TD-2/PP-TD-7 are open in the file F-8 edits).
risks.mitigation: PLAN-AS-12: read the prompt from the assembled envelope, not from MirrorUiState. History then records exactly what the agent received, whatever PP-TD-2 does, and F-8 neither depends on nor blocks that fix.

functional.text: Provide a History tab listing every batch ever sent, grouped by time period, each row showing a thumbnail crop, title/summary, timestamp, and a status chip (e.g. Fixed, In progress).

On every successful AnnotationHandoff.publish (F-7), persist a new Batch record (frozen frame copy, per-annotation crop copies, hierarchy dump, prompt, sessionId, sentAtMs, device info) to the local Room database with initial status Sent.

Copy the frozen frame PNG and each per-annotation crop PNG from the handoff slot into app-owned storage at persist time, because F-7 prunes every handoff-slot image directory except the latest after each publish and a bare path reference would go stale.
Render History rows grouped under Today / Yesterday / Older headers, based on the batch's local calendar day relative to now, newest batch first within each group.

Compute each row's 44x44 thumbnail by running the existing crop() algorithm (pad=18, bw=bh=40) against the union bounding box of all of the batch's annotation rects. IMPLEMENTATION OF RECORD: reimplemented as the pure thumbnailRect(union, frameSize, designPad = 18f, designWidth = 296f) because the shipped cropWindow() is a 14f/84x72 render-window builder, not an encoder (PLAN-AS-1); the encoded result is capped at 128px and rendered into HistoryRow's shipped 56dp plate (PLAN-AS-4).

Render each row's title as the batch's first annotation's comment text (ellipsised, single line) and its meta line as '<n> notes . <HH:mm sent time> . #<last 4 hex chars of batch id>'. CORRECTION OF RECORD: implemented as (id.hashCode() and 0xFFFF).toString(16).padStart(4, '0') — mintSessionId returns '<deviceId>-f<frameId>-<sentAtMs>' in decimal, so the literal wording is not satisfiable.

Render a status chip with a tone dot per BatchStatus value (Sent, In progress, Fixed, Verified, Follow-up sent), matching the design's tone mapping; Sent shares Verified's neutral tone since the prototype defines no distinct tone for it.
Show a Verify button only on rows with status Fixed; clicking it invokes a caller-supplied callback (no-op by default). The diff/verify logic itself is out of scope (F-9).

Expose a BatchRepository.updateStatus(batchId, BatchStatus) API for a future consumer (F-9) to drive In progress / Fixed / Verified / Follow-up sent transitions; F-8 itself never calls it beyond the initial Sent write.
Show History as the third segment of RectifyWindow's existing inspector tab strip, with a badge equal to the count of batches currently in In progress status (hidden when zero).
Show a footer line 'claude . session <sessionId>' sourced from the most recently persisted batch's sessionId; project path is omitted because AnnotationEnvelope carries no such field.
Keep all persisted batches visible indefinitely; no delete or retention UI ships in this spec.

nonFunctional.text: All mirror stream data, screenshots, hierarchy dumps, and payloads stay local to the machine; no network egress beyond localhost MCP communication.
History and batch metadata persist locally and survive app restarts.
The History list renders via a lazily-virtualized list (Compose LazyColumn) so UI render cost stays independent of total persisted batch count.
Copying frame and crop PNGs to durable per-batch storage at publish time runs off the UI thread, consistent with AnnotationHandoff's existing suspend contract.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given batches have been sent previously, when the History tab is opened, then batches are grouped by time period, each showing thumbnail, summary, timestamp, and status chip.
Given History contains at least one batch, when the app is quit and relaunched, then all batches, their status chips, stored frozen frames, and per-annotation records are still present and openable.
Given the History tab badge, when zero batches have status In progress, then no badge is shown on the tab; when N batches are In progress, the badge shows N.

Given a batch has more than one annotation, when its History row thumbnail is generated, then the crop is computed from the union bounding box of all of the batch's annotation rects, not just the first.
Given a batch's status, when its History row renders, then the Verify button is shown only for status Fixed and is absent for every other status.
Given at least one batch has been persisted, when the History list footer renders, then it shows 'claude . session <id>' sourced from the most recently persisted batch's sessionId.

Given F-7 prunes the handoff slot's image files after each publish, when a batch is persisted, then its frame and crop images have already been copied into app-owned storage so they remain available after subsequent sends and app restarts.

architecture.approach: One persistence vertical (entity + child entity + DAO + datasource + repository + mapper + two use cases) hung off the existing mirror surface, with one new side effect inside MirrorViewModel.resolveAndSend() and one new field on MirrorUiState. Write-after-success in its own failure domain; read through a bare Flow collected in the container init; render with a keyed LazyColumn over shipped design-system components; two edits in RectifyWindow.kt.
architecture.rationale: Persist-after-success was chosen over persist-before-publish (would show a lying 'Sent' row for a batch the agent never received, contradicting FR-26), over sharing publish's runCatching (a full disk could reduce SendPhase.Failed for a send that actually succeeded — the one outcome explicitly ruled out), and over a detached fire-and-forget launch (makes SC-16's row racy against the toast and escapes the test harness's advanceUntilIdle discipline) — for one extra .onFailure line. The brainstorm's key realisation holds: assembleEnvelope already returns (envelope, images) as in-memory values and held.bytes/held.bitmap are locals, so F-8 never reads anything back from ~/.rectify/handoff and FR-27/AC-38 are satisfied by construction, not by racing the pruner. A normalised child table beats a JSON blob because the blob would embed AnnotationEnvelope (documented as wire-breaking) in durable storage, store knowingly dead cropPaths, and drag kotlinx-serialization into presentation-feature-mirror; the child table costs ~30 lines and makes F-9's per-annotation 'resolved' flag a column add. A thumbnail BLOB beats thumb.png + path because a commonMain composable cannot read a file, so a path would require a whole new expect/actual image-loading seam for a single plate — and the BLOB makes 'the row survives manual file deletion' structural rather than defensive. The thumbnail is cropped AND downscaled in commonMain before it reaches CropEncoder (PLAN-AS-8): AwtCropEncoder was re-read at refine and genuinely only crops, so the alternative was a ~250 KB BLOB per row; scaling first keeps one encoder seam, adds no DI, and makes the encode cheaper because toAwtImage() then allocates 64 KB instead of 10 MB. BatchFileStore as a fun-interface Koin seam matches two existing precedents (CropEncoder, HandoffSourcesProvider), avoids adding okio/kotlinx-io for three file writes, and is the only option that lets SC-18 be unit-tested without a real disk.

errorStates.behavior: No persisted batches: MirrorHistoryTab early-returns an empty state copying MirrorNotesTab's shape, with mirror_history_empty. The footer is hidden when there is no batch (AC-37 is conditioned on 'at least one batch persisted').

No spinner. MirrorUiState.history defaults to emptyList() and the first Flow emission replaces it, typically within a frame of the panel opening; a transient empty state is indistinguishable from the genuine empty state and needs no extra UI.
DB read failure: HistoryRepositoryImpl.observe() is guarded with .catch { log.w(it); emit(emptyList()) }, so the tab degrades to the empty state and the mirror surface never crashes.

DB write failure (SQLiteException, disk full, locked file): mapped to Failure.Technical.Database by resultLauncher, returned as Result.failure, consumed in resolveAndSend with .onFailure { log.w } only. SendPhase is untouched, no side effect is posted, the send still reports success. One batch is silently missing from History — the accepted trade.

File write failure (SC-18): BatchFileStore returns null instead of throwing; the row is still inserted with dirPath/framePath/hierarchyPath = null and its thumbPng intact, so it renders completely. Only F-9's future diff needs the frame, and it existence-checks at use time.

Thumbnail unavailable: cropAndScale returns null on a degenerate rect, or CropEncoder returns null (Android/iOS stand-in, any AWT/ImageIO failure). thumbPng is null and HistoryRow draws its bare chrome plate. No separate placeholder asset exists or is needed.

Stored image path whose file the user deleted by hand: the row renders unchanged, because rendering reads only DB columns (thumbnail BLOB included) and performs zero filesystem reads. This is structural, not defensive.

Batch with zero annotations: unblocked by canSend today, but unionRect returns null, the thumbnail encode is skipped, thumbPng is null, the title falls back to neutral localised copy and the meta line reads '0 notes'. Nothing crashes.

DB open failure on first launch (unwritable ~/.rectify, corrupt file): Room builds lazily and opens on first query, so the failure surfaces inside the guarded observe() Flow (empty tab + log.w) or inside resultLauncher on the first write (logged), never as a Koin graph construction crash. DatabaseBuilder.desktop mkdirs() the directory first so the common case cannot fail.
Same-millisecond id collision: @Insert(onConflict = REPLACE) overwrites the parent row and its cascaded children rather than throwing.

performanceBudget.target: <= 8 KB per row (<=128px longest edge, PNG). Enforced by cropAndScale's maxEdgePx before encoding and asserted by ThumbnailBitmapTest; re-checked once against a real 1080x2400 send in the demo.

AwtCropEncoder calls toAwtImage() on whatever it is handed — <=128px in means a ~64 KB BufferedImage instead of the ~10 MB a full frame would allocate. The scale step makes the encode cheaper, not more expensive.
<= 150 ms for a 3-annotation batch (thumbnail encode + ~1 MB of file writes + one transaction), inside an already multi-second operation; all of it off the UI thread (NFR-14).
< 100 ms per emission on desktop, with queries on Dispatchers.IO via setQueryCoroutineContext.
<= 10 MB of thumbnail bytes in MirrorUiState.

Independent of total batch count (NFR-13) — LazyColumn composes only visible rows, items are keyed by entry id, and each PNG decode is memoised with remember(entry.id). The footer sits outside the scroll (design's flex:none).
One state emission per send (not per frame); no polling, no midnight timer.
Unbounded by design (accepted ceiling); ~0.5-2 MB per batch of frame + crops + hierarchy. Recorded in a `ponytail:` comment in BatchFileStore with the age/count-cap upgrade path.

No AAPT-style apostrophe escapes (regression fixed in dae0893). Every piece of copy in MirrorHistoryTab resolves through stringResource — presentation-core-ui kit components take copy as parameters and never depend on presentation-core-localisation, which is exactly why the feature module is the stringResource call site.

dataHandling: NFR-4: nothing leaves the machine. No HTTP client exists in the dependency graph of any module F-8 touches, and none is added (network.md confirms ktor is declared-but-unused scaffolding); storage is the local filesystem plus a local SQLite file.
All app-owned data consolidates under ~/.rectify (rectify.db + history/ + the existing handoff/), so a user who wants to erase Rectify's data deletes one directory.
Hierarchy XML can be hundreds of KB and may contain on-screen text: it is written as a file inside the batch directory, never into a list-query column, and never logged.
Annotation comments and prompts are persisted in TEXT columns and never emitted to logs; log lines carry batch ids and paths only.
Batch directory names are sanitised with [^A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by '_' so a device id can never escape the history root via path traversal (PLAN-AS-6).
permissions: Desktop filesystem access to the user's home directory only — already exercised by F-7's handoff slot; no new OS permission, no new entitlement, no network permission.
privacy: No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reporting carries annotation text, prompts, screenshots or hierarchy dumps.
No retention policy ships (FR-36): data persists until the user deletes ~/.rectify/history. This is a deliberate, recorded ceiling; a future retention spec owns the delete affordance.
File permissions are whatever java.io creates under the user's home (owner-readable); no attempt is made to broaden them.

survey.question: C-1: how is the History thumbnail kept to a few KB, given AwtCropEncoder was re-read at refine and genuinely only crops (getSubimage) with no scale step?
options: Crop AND downscale to <=128px in commonMain (ImageBitmap(w,h) + androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Canvas + drawImageRect with FilterQuality.Medium), then hand the small bitmap to the UNCHANGED CropEncoder — no new DI seam, gated by a desktopTest asserting <=128px and <=8 KB
Add a desktopMain AwtThumbnailEncoder sibling (getSubimage + getScaledInstance) bound behind a Koin qualifier
Add a maxEdgePx parameter to CropEncoder.encode and change all three platform bindings
survey.answer: Crop AND downscale to <=128px in commonMain (ImageBitmap(w,h) + androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Canvas + drawImageRect with FilterQuality.Medium), then hand the small bitmap to the UNCHANGED CropEncoder — no new DI seam, gated by a desktopTest asserting <=128px and <=8 KB
survey.rationale: All three APIs are commonMain compose-ui-graphics, so no expect/actual and no new binding appears, and F-7's merged CropEncoder contract is untouched. It is also strictly cheaper than the naive path: AwtCropEncoder calls toAwtImage() on whatever it is handed, so a 128px input allocates ~64 KB instead of ~10 MB. The risk of the common Canvas path misbehaving is converted from an open question into one desktopTest with a single named trigger for the AWT fallback, rather than left as a coin flip at implementation time.

survey.question: Where do the two Room @Entity classes live, given database.md says core/entity/ but package-layout.md reserves core/ for internal-only declarations and the entities are the public HistoryDataSource's wire type?
options: source/entity/ (public) plus a one-line amendment to .claude/rules/database.md recording the exception
core/entity/ (internal) plus a parallel set of public DTOs copied field-by-field at the datasource boundary (~60 lines)
core/entity/ and make HistoryDataSource internal, moving the repository impl into data-database-impl
survey.answer: source/entity/ (public) plus a one-line amendment to .claude/rules/database.md recording the exception
survey.rationale: explicitApi() and package-layout.md make core/ genuinely internal-only, so a public datasource cannot name a core/ type. Option 2 pays ~60 lines of hand-copied DTOs plus a second mapper for zero behavioural gain, and option 3 collapses the data/repository module boundary the whole architecture rests on. The rules file is the thing that is slightly wrong here, and a one-line amendment is the smallest honest fix.

survey.question: HistoryRow ships a 56dp thumbnail plate while the design quotes 44x44. What ships in F-8?
options: Reuse HistoryRow as-is at 56dp; encode the thumbnail at <=128px so it stays crisp in the larger plate
Parameterise HistoryRow's plate size and pass 44.dp from MirrorHistoryTab
Change the design-system constant to 44dp for every consumer
survey.answer: Reuse HistoryRow as-is at 56dp; encode the thumbnail at <=128px so it stays crisp in the larger plate
survey.rationale: No AC mentions the plate dimension, and HistoryRow is a registered, previewed design-system molecule with other prospective consumers. Option 2 adds a parameter for one call site; option 3 changes shipped visuals outside F-8's scope and needs the design-system owner's gate. The 128px encode means the 12dp difference costs nothing visually, so the question can stay a design-system backlog item instead of blocking this spec.
